title: I will allure her (Hosea 2)
hook: God as a hurt husband who leads his people into the wilderness to speak to her heart

segments.voice: Yesterday, Ezekiel's valley: bone to its bone, and then the ruach, breath, from the four winds. Your line was can these bones live. What small thing did you do for the dry one? Day four hundred twenty-six.

Hosea's message came to him as a marriage. The book dates him by the kings he lived under, among them Jeroboam of Israel, and it opens with God telling him to marry a woman who would be unfaithful to him. Her name was Gomer. They had three children, and God gave each child a name that was a sermon. A son called Jezrahel, after a valley of bloodshed. A daughter called Without mercy. A son called Not my people. Every time he called them in for dinner, he said a prophecy out loud. Hosea's own kitchen table became the picture of a broken covenant.
screen: `A PROPHET HANDED A MARRIAGE.` → `GOMER, AND THREE NAMES.` → `WITHOUT MERCY. NOT MY PEOPLE.`

segments.voice: Chapter two sounds like a divorce court. The husband is God, the wife is the people, and the charge is that she ran after other lovers, the Baals, the local gods, and gave them the credit for her grain and wine and oil. The anger is real, and it goes on for verses. Then comes a word you'd expect to lead into the sentence: therefore. And here's what follows it, in the Douay-Rheims: "Therefore, behold I will allure her, and will lead her into the wilderness: and I will speak to her heart." Not punish her. Allure her. Win her back. And the wilderness isn't exile; it's where the love story began, when God led the people out of Egypt and they were young. Speak to her heart is a Hebrew phrase for speaking tenderly, the way you talk to someone you've hurt or who has hurt you. Joseph speaks to his brothers' hearts when he forgives them in Genesis. Isaiah is told to speak to the heart of Jerusalem in the comfort chapter we read a week ago. And by the end of the chapter, God promises: I will espouse thee to me for ever, in justice and mercy and faithfulness. The children's names get reversed. Without mercy will be shown mercy. Not my people will hear: thou art my people. Some Catholic writers have read Hosea alongside the Song of Songs, as God's love for his people and for each soul. Some readers today find the husband-and-wife picture hard, with the wife cast as the one at fault and the anger so fierce, and they wrestle with that honestly. Either way, the turn is there in the text: after all of it, therefore, tenderness.
screen: `A CHARGE LIKE A DIVORCE COURT.` · `THEREFORE: I WILL ALLURE HER.` · `SPEAK TO HER HEART: SPEAK TENDERLY.` · `NOT MY PEOPLE BECOMES MY PEOPLE.` · then, large: `I WILL SPEAK TO HER HEART.`

segments.voice: Here's the practice: let God speak tenderly. Settle, and breathe. Think of the last time you got something wrong, and listen to the voice that started up in your head afterward. Is it a judge? A sigh? A list? Now try the other voice Hosea describes, the one that says therefore and then turns gentle. Picture being led somewhere quiet, away from the noise, and spoken to as someone who is still loved. If you pray, you can simply sit and let God speak to your heart, without rushing to answer. If you don't, try speaking to yourself the way you'd speak to a friend. The bell holds the time.
Gomer. Hosea's unfaithful wife, whose story became God's promise to lead his people into the wilderness and win them back with tenderness. Today's word.
Your line: speak to her heart. Today, when you have something hard to say to someone, say it to their heart: gently, and in a quiet place. Day four hundred twenty-six.

howItsDone: Catholics hear Hosea's promise to speak to the heart in the Mass readings, and Catholic retreats sometimes take it up, describing days of silence as being led into the wilderness to listen.

myth: after the anger, God plans to lead his people into the wilderness to punish them
to allure her, and speak to her heart. the wilderness is where it began.

Jezrahel, Without mercy, and Not my people; the names are reversed by the end of chapter two.

fork.setup: you're the hurt husband in Hosea's story. she ran after other lovers and forgot who loved her. the verse begins: therefore. what comes next?
options: therefore I will shut the door for good.
therefore I will allure her, lead her into the wilderness, and speak to her heart.
therefore I will send her away with nothing.
fork.reveal: the word you'd expect to bring the punishment brings tenderness instead: I will allure her, and speak to her heart.

original.note: Hebrew: heart, the center of thought and will as well as feeling. to speak 'upon the heart' is to speak tenderly.

trapdoor: what you thought: allure sounds like seduction.
what it means: after a long charge of unfaithfulness, God promises to win his people back, leading them to the wilderness where their love began.
what a scholar hears: dibber al-lev, speak upon the heart, the idiom of Genesis 50:21 and Isaiah 40:2; and the children's names Lo-ruhamah and Lo-ammi reversed.
recall: a great general, and a leper
